meta.storyTitle: Qualify installation, upgrades and lifecycle across platforms

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Choose a1: one shared user-level installer/manager with bundle and dev delivery adapters. Install launched from either IDE runs the same public platform installer script interactively in a visible terminal; the script owns prompts and output. IDE-specific installation wizards and hidden background installs are excluded. Lifecycle, migration, runtime and privilege constraints remain shared and unchanged. Successful interactive installation hands the same terminal directly to the installed insrc TUI after daemon readiness; it does not finish at an idle shell.

consumedContracts.name: Installation and release identity
consumedContracts.purpose: One installation owns one selected delivery mode, zero or one active release and zero or one unresolved operation. Release identities are immutable; the controller metadata never stores application DB contents.

consumedContracts.name: Manager command and operation state
consumedContracts.purpose: A private-runtime command runner serves both IDEs when daemon is running, stopped or blocked. One OS-backed exclusive lock serializes all mutating operations per installation; controller records and bounded progress are shared across clients. Interactive install is invoked by the shared script in the terminal. The structured manager protocol remains for ordinary control/status; the IDE does not drive installation prompts through it. The 'install' action is reserved exclusively for the shared bootstrap/installer script executing inside the interactive terminal. VS Code/JetBrains adapters must never invoke ManagerAction.install directly or drive its prompts through this protocol; they only launch/focus the terminal and observe completion/readiness. The s1 LLD must state and enforce this caller restriction.

consumedContracts.name: Dependency report and consent
consumedContracts.purpose: Foundation contract separates required private Node, Ollama availability and advisory agent CLI detection from their platform implementations in s3; IDEs cannot infer consent from plugin updates.
consumedContracts.interfaceSketch:
interface DependencyReport { runtimeReady: boolean; ollama: 'ready' | 'installed-not-running' | 'missing' | 'unavailable'; ollamaInstallOffer?: { id: string; destination: string; version: string }; agents: { claude: boolean; codex: boolean; vibe: boolean }; recommendations: string[]; blockers: string[] }
interface DependencyDecision { offerId: string; choice: 'install' | 'decline' }

consumedContracts.name: Daemon shutdown and readiness
consumedContracts.purpose: The selected daemon admits shutdown over its local JSON-RPC endpoint only. Acknowledgement is not exit completion. Readiness reports instance/release identity and startup gating; immediate escalation is an explicit second request.

consumedContracts.name: Ordered upgrade hook delegation
consumedContracts.purpose: Owned by foundational s1 because delivery preparation, startup guard and s5 runner all require the same hook manifest. s5 implements execution. Hooks run in-process inside a candidate daemon migration-only process that exclusively owns data; manager and IDE never open LMDB/Lance.

consumedContracts.name: Local transport and explicit installation home
consumedContracts.purpose: All consumers resolve the same installation home and endpoint. Unix retains daemon.sock; Windows uses a per-user/per-installation named pipe. The manager's Node bridge supplies JetBrains Windows transport without changing application RPC payloads.

consumedContracts.name: Shared terminal installer launch
consumedContracts.purpose: Foundation-owned contract makes manual and both IDE installation entrypoints identical. IDE adapters only open/focus a terminal and invoke the same script; the terminal owns the interaction and durable operation state/readiness determines success. On successful install/readiness the shared script releases installation ownership and launches the installed TUI in the same terminal; failure/cancel does not launch it.

boundary.internal: Private isolated VM/runner fixtures, target matrix evidence and release qualification results, including real Windows named-pipe behavior and preservation of host v2 daemon. Terminal-install parity checks cover each IDE and manual invocation, paths with spaces/Unicode, missing terminal support, declined Ollama, Ctrl+C/close, duplicate windows, retained output and readiness-confirmed completion. Verify successful install enters TUI in the original terminal, install lock is released before TUI use, TUI exit leaves daemon running, and failure/cancellation never opens TUI. DEF traceability: E20261123c3d71313:S008:FR001 and this story's DEF acceptance criteria apply unchanged.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Own the foundational manifest, controller/operation/consent/hook/transport contracts because every branch already depends on s1. Private implementation covers bootstrap, runtime/payload integrity, bundle preparation/publication, platform lock adapter and atomic install records. Later stories implement lifecycle, checks and hooks behind these contracts. The canonical scripts and interactive installer mode are shared with manual invocation and both IDEs; terminal prompts and durable results are part of this foundation. Include the selected release's installed TUI entry/assets in the payload and default successful interactive installer-to-TUI handoff. The s1 LLD must explicitly reserve ManagerAction.install to the shared terminal bootstrap script and forbid IDE-adapter invocation. DEF traceability: E20261123c3d71313:S001:FR001 and this story's DEF acceptance criteria apply unchanged.

Private dev checkout/branch sync, lockfile installation and native build preparation; returns the same immutable prepared candidate. It does not define a second lifecycle or migration engine. Include the selected release's installed TUI entry/assets in the payload and default successful interactive installer-to-TUI handoff. DEF traceability: E20261123c3d71313:S002:FR001 and this story's DEF acceptance criteria apply unchanged.

Private platform dependency detection, user-level Ollama installation and agent CLI recommendations. It implements foundational reports/consent and never auto-installs agent CLIs. DEF traceability: E20261123c3d71313:S003:FR001 and this story's DEF acceptance criteria apply unchanged.

Private daemon start/readiness, boot guard integration, shutdown drain/immediate exit and exit-completion launcher wrapper; transport is shared. No delivery sync/build on start and no signal/PID daemon control. DEF traceability: E20261123c3d71313:S004:FR001 and this story's DEF acceptance criteria apply unchanged.

Private ordered migration runner, daemon migration-only mode, blocked-state persistence, interrupted-run validation and explicit retry. Hooks alone choose data changes and recovery policy. DEF traceability: E20261123c3d71313:S005:FR001 and this story's DEF acceptance criteria apply unchanged.

Private VS Code native terminal open/focus/launch integration, duplicate-action handling and post-install reconnect. It invokes the shared script and leaves all install prompts/output in that terminal, including after failure. Existing ordinary lifecycle and upgrade-consent UI remains thin. Successful installation automatically enters the installed TUI in that same terminal; the IDE only reconnects/status-checks and does not require a second click. DEF traceability: E20261123c3d71313:S006:FR001 and this story's DEF acceptance criteria apply unchanged.

Private JetBrains native terminal open/focus/launch integration with the same script, stdin/output and post-install readiness behavior as VS Code; no independent wizard or hidden install. Preserve background activation/control and Windows IPC bridge for ordinary daemon operations. Successful installation automatically enters the installed TUI in that same terminal; the IDE only reconnects/status-checks and does not require a second click. DEF traceability: E20261123c3d71313:S007:FR001 and this story's DEF acceptance criteria apply unchanged.

nonFunctional.performance: Targets: local read-only inspection/reachability <=3 seconds; activation never blocks IDE UI. Progress/phase changes emit within 1 second after state changes. Ready startup target <=15 seconds excluding dependency/model initialization; startup probe deadline 30 seconds. Default graceful wait 60 seconds with configurable user deadline; timeout reports uncertainty and never silently escalates. Downloads/builds/hooks have per-operation budgets and progress, not an arbitrary task retry loop.
nonFunctional.security: No elevated commands, global PATH edits, user credential capture, LLM calls for dependency detection or shell-interpolated actions. Verify payload/runtime digests and targets, reject archive traversal/symlink escapes and module paths outside candidate payload. Local endpoints are user-scoped, capability-protected where needed; bind operation/instance/release identity. Signing deferred and no cryptographic authenticity claim from unsigned digest metadata. No IDE prompt automation or credential/input capture; terminal launch preserves argument boundaries. User-visible script identity matches manual release assets.
nonFunctional.observability: Structured operationId/installationId/from-to identity, platform/runtime/digest, phase/hook/stage, duration and actionable error code. Bounded NDJSON to IDE, logs in installation home with rotation; no credentials/tokens or full migration data. Report explicitly which platform/native checks passed and which were unavailable. Interactive installation prints human-readable phases and errors directly in the terminal. The terminal is retained after completion/failure; its output is not scraped or treated as success evidence.
nonFunctional.durability: OS-backed mutation exclusivity plus atomic versioned controller records. Prepared payloads immutable; candidate data mutation is daemon-owned only. Record hook run-started before execution and require test before completion; failures/interruption retain blocked startup. Retry never substitutes a different candidate or starts the predecessor after data changes automatically. Installation completion and lock release precede the interactive TUI session. TUI exit/launch failure cannot roll back the completed installation or keep an installation lock held.

summary.prose: Qualification proves both delivery modes and both IDE integrations on isolated real platforms. Each result names the exact release/runtime, environment and scenario, with unavailable coverage kept separate from passes. This story supplies evidence and release gates, not another implementation of the installer.

dataModelChanges.details: New private test record contains profileId, scenarioId, OS/version/kernel, process and kernel architectures, virtualization/translation mode, filesystem, CPU/GPU context where relevant, IDE product/version/terminal engine, runtime version/ABI, source commit, script/manifest/archive/native-binding digests, timestamps, expected/observed behavior, result(pass/fail/unavailable), diagnostics/log refs and cleanup outcome. One profile has many scenario results; one result binds exactly one candidate identity and environment. No new public daemon API or DB entity is introduced. Proposed test/evidence boundaries: src/installer/__tests__/qualification.test.ts and this story's evidence directory.

Linux primary: isolated Ubuntu 24.04 OrbStack arm64 and x64 guests, recreating previously deleted test VMs when execution is authorized. Record x64 translation; native x64 Linux runner supplies architecture-sensitive gaps. macOS arm64 primary: existing insrc-macos-arm64 UTM VM on external storage; current guest success does not prove the declared minimum OS baseline. Use an isolated macOS x64 runner/host and baseline-matching environment for Intel/minimum-version coverage. Windows: Windows 11 ARM64 UTM guest for native ARM64/explicit x64-emulation cases plus actual Windows x64 runner for native x64 modules/pipe behavior. These are selected execution environments, not claims they exist or tests have passed. Missing environment/package support marks target unavailable and prevents advertising that target.

For both bundle and dev delivery: clean install with no/wrong host Node; exact successor upgrade; unchanged delivery/ref selection; shared terminal/manual script parity; readiness-confirmed same-terminal TUI; start/no-build; graceful stop; explicit immediate override; restart/actual exit proof; migration skip/success/check-run-test failure/interruption/retry; dependency existing/missing/decline/install; zero/one/many agent recommendations; concurrent windows; Unicode/space/metacharacter paths; download/digest/target/archive corruption; source dirty/build failure; stale offers; and corrupt controller/journal recovery. Each IDE separately proves native terminal visibility/focus, ordinary control, startup autostart, explicit upgrade accept/dismiss including plugin updates, blocked migration UI and close/cancel behavior. Cross-review regression matrix explicitly includes: two clients escalate immediate while graceful operation lock remains held; first migration admission versus ordinary startup; manager death with live candidate at every journal boundary, no second runner, exact journal/exit reconciliation; correlated Windows per-request pre-write cancel, first-write race, helper death and protocol mismatch. Record full owner/session/operation identities with secrets redacted. The sc2/sc4/sc6 amendments are approved; consumer designs must carry current effective-HLD metadata before this matrix executes. Require migration-wrapper durable receipts on natural success, hook failure and manager death, including crash before/after receipt fsync/publication and mismatched session/nonce/digest. Require protocol-2 hello/ready success, 3-second timeout, malformed/duplicate/wrong version/nonce/early outcome and unsupported-helper cases with zero pre-ready application sends.

Every fixture uses explicit isolated home, endpoint, operation identity and test repository registration. Record/assert resolved home/socket/pipe before mutation and refuse the host default home or active host v2 endpoint. Native module imports and representative LMDB/Lance/DuckDB/parser paths run only in owned disposable test/daemon processes; graph fixtures register repositories through the daemon contract before inserts. No model downloads or cloud LLM requests are needed for installer qualification. Run CPU-only dependency smoke when GPU drivers are absent; never install drivers or elevated packages.

Use bounded canonical Node coordinator, existing JetBrains JUnit and native IDE harnesses. Test timeouts are failures/unavailable—not successful shutdown—and generic test-child cleanup is recorded separately from product IPC-only lifecycle proof. Preserve exact logs/artifact identities and host fingerprint; redact auth/capabilities. A target passes only when all required target/mode/IDE scenarios and native probes match exact candidate bytes. Missing/failed/translated-only baseline evidence blocks that target's qualification; signing is not introduced. A later changed source/archive/runtime invalidates prior evidence. All sibling implementation issues remain owned by their stories.

errorCases.scenario: Missing real platform or native dependency
errorCases.detection: Profile setup/native probe cannot execute on declared target/baseline.
errorCases.response: Record unavailable with concrete blocker; do not mark passed or publish support.

errorCases.detection: Candidate/runtime/script/native digests or environment do not match profile.
errorCases.response: Reject evidence for acceptance and rerun the exact candidate.
errorCases.userImpact: Old success cannot authorize new bytes.

errorCases.detection: Resolved home/endpoint equals host v2/default or another profile's ownership.

errorCases.scenario: Scenario times out or cleanup fails
errorCases.detection: Coordinator budget expires or owned resources remain unresolved.
errorCases.response: Failed/unavailable scenario plus cleanup diagnostics; no silent background loop.
errorCases.userImpact: Test suite does not claim lifecycle success from forced cleanup.

edgeCases.expected: Report per-target status; do not collapse into all-platform green.

alternativesConsidered.name: Explicit matrix with immutable evidence records
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Each target/scenario records exact candidate, environment and observed result.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
Run bounded test scenarios against disposable installations and record pass/fail/unavailable per exact OS/architecture/runtime/source/archive identity. Reuse the canonical test coordinator and native IDE sandboxes.

Publication/readiness is gated by complete matching evidence for the advertised target; unit/fixture results and translated-host results are never silently promoted to native coverage.
pros: Evidence remains tied to exact bytes and declared target.
cons: Needs actual provisioned OS/IDE environments; fake-only CI cannot finish acceptance.

alternativesConsidered.name: One aggregate cross-platform smoke result
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Run a common smoke script and publish one consolidated status.
alternativesConsidered.approach:
Use the same isolated scenarios but aggregate all outcomes into one report after runners finish. Detailed logs can still be retained per runner.

To meet the HLD, this design still needs explicit target/provenance fields and unavailable statuses, so the aggregate adds no simplification to the underlying evidence model.
pros: One top-level result is easy to display.
cons: A single green summary can obscure target and translated/native gaps unless it duplicates the explicit matrix.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: An aggregate smoke result does not remove the required target/provenance matrix and risks hiding missing native coverage.
